business_problem: GM wanted to replace a sequential, handoff-heavy vehicle development process that slowed feedback, required too much physical iteration, and exposed programs to late-stage surprises across design, engineering, validation, and manufacturing.
solution_summary: GM built an in-house, virtual-first vehicle development workflow around a shared digital foundation and integrated digital thread that carries data across design, engineering, validation, and manufacturing. Early in the process, AI is applied to hand-drawn concept sketches to generate many more design variations plus teaser animation in less than a day, giving teams faster design-space exploration. An AI-powered virtual wind tunnel then lets designers and aerodynamicists evaluate drag effects from surface changes in real time. Deeper in engineering, co-simulation links physics-based plant models with virtual controllers in a closed-loop environment so software and hardware behavior can be validated before physical hardware is available. For safety work, virtual crash simulation uses advanced machine learning to compress roof crush analysis from hours to minutes. In manufacturing, immersive XR and augmented reality help teams review assembly sequences, ergonomics, tooling placement, clearance, and access before installation, reducing prototype dependence and shortening commissioning.

data_flow: Hand-drawn concept sketches and decades of engineering data feed GM’s shared digital foundation, where AI expands design options and the AI-powered virtual wind tunnel evaluates aerodynamic effects. The digital thread carries updates into co-simulation, which connects plant models and virtual controllers for closed-loop validation, then into virtual crash simulation for safety analysis. Manufacturing teams consume the same evolving models through XR and AR to validate assembly, ergonomics, and tooling before physical installation.
business_outcome: GM reports faster feedback loops, more concurrent collaboration, more targeted physical validation, fewer late surprises, faster plant readiness, and higher-quality, more reliable vehicle programs.
